title: Things to Do in Nainital: Lake, Viewpoints & the Kumaon Lake District
seoTitle: Things to Do in Nainital: Lake, Viewpoints & More | Kudozz Club
description: Things to do in Nainital: boating on Naini Lake, the Naina Devi Temple, Mall Road, the ropeway to Snow View, Tiffin Top and Naina Peak walks, and day trips to Bhimtal, Sattal and Mukteshwar.
dek: A green lake ringed by forested hills, a Mall Road built for evening strolls, and a chain of quieter lakes and orchards just beyond town.
searchIntent: Families, couples and weekenders from Delhi NCR planning two to three days in Nainital and the nearby lakes.

hero.alt: Naini Lake and the Naina Devi Temple, Nainital
hero.caption: Naini Lake and Naina Devi Temple

intro: Nainital is a hill town at about 2,000 metres in the Kumaon hills of Uttarakhand, built around the pear-shaped Naini Lake. It was developed as a summer retreat by the British in the 1840s, and later served as the summer capital of the United Provinces. Today it is one of the most popular hill stations in North India, especially for families from Delhi NCR.

Most things to do in Nainital are around the lake and on the ridges above it: boating, the Naina Devi Temple, the Mall Road, the ropeway and short walks to viewpoints. The real advantage of a longer stay is the Kumaon lake district nearby, with Bhimtal, Sattal and Naukuchiatal, and orchard towns such as Mukteshwar.
Two days covers the town; three to four lets you explore the lakes around it. Weekends and summer holidays are very busy.
quickAnswer: Go boating or sailing on Naini Lake
Stroll the Mall Road in the evening
Ride the ropeway to Snow View Point
Walk or ride to Tiffin Top (Dorothy's Seat)
Hike to Naina Peak (China Peak) for Himalayan views
Take a day trip to Bhimtal, Sattal and Naukuchiatal
Visit Mukteshwar for orchards and Himalayan views

items.name: Go boating on Naini Lake
body: Rowing boats, pedal boats and yachts are available from the jetties on the Mall Road and near the Flats. The Nainital Boat Club, one of the oldest in India, organises sailing. A boat in the early morning, when the lake is still and the town is quiet, is especially pleasant.

items.name: Visit Naina Devi Temple
body: The Naina Devi Temple, on the northern shore of the lake, is dedicated to the goddess from whom Nainital takes its name and is counted among the Shakti Peethas. The Nanda Devi Mela, held here in late summer, is the town's main festival.

items.name: Stroll the Mall Road

image.alt: Mall Road along Naini Lake, Nainital
image.caption: Mall Road

body: The Mall Road runs along the lake between Mallital and Tallital, lined with shops, cafés and hotels. It is at its liveliest in the evening, when families walk the promenade and the lakeside lights come on. Look for candle shops, a Nainital speciality, and Tibetan markets near the Flats.

facts.Good to know: Vehicle restrictions apply at busy times

items.name: See the Flats and St John in the Wilderness
body: The Flats, a large open ground at Mallital, created after a landslide in 1880, is used for sports and fairs. St John in the Wilderness, a 19th-century Gothic church in the forest above the lake, is one of the town's oldest buildings.

items.name: Ride the ropeway to Snow View
body: A cable car runs from Mallital up to Snow View Point, from where, on clear days, you can see peaks of the Himalaya such as Nanda Devi. Mornings in October and November and after rain give the clearest views. Queues can be long in summer.

items.name: Walk to Tiffin Top
body: Tiffin Top (Dorothy's Seat), on Ayarpatta Hill, is a viewpoint reached by a pleasant forest walk of about 4 km from the town, or by pony. It gives a wide view over the lake and the surrounding hills. Land's End, nearby, looks over the valley towards Khurpatal.

items.name: Hike to Naina Peak
body: Naina Peak (China Peak) is the highest point around Nainital at about 2,600 metres. The hike through oak and rhododendron forest takes a couple of hours, and on clear days it offers a broad view of the Himalayan range. Go with a guide or local directions, and start early.

items.name: Explore the Eco Cave Gardens
body: A set of small interconnected caves and gardens on the hillside, the Eco Cave Gardens are a hit with children, who crawl through the narrow caves named after animals. There is a musical fountain show in the evening.

items.name: Visit the zoo and Raj Bhavan
body: The High Altitude Zoo on Sher ka Danda hill houses Himalayan animals such as red pandas, leopards and Himalayan black bears. The Raj Bhavan, a Gothic-style governor's residence from 1900, has guided tours and a golf course.

items.name: Go birdwatching at Kilbury and Pangot
body: The oak forests of Kilbury and the village of Pangot, about 15 km from Nainital, are among the best birding areas in the Kumaon hills. Species such as the khalij pheasant, Himalayan griffon and several laughingthrushes are seen here. Small homestays and lodges at Pangot are a quiet alternative to staying in town.

items.name: Watch sunset from Hanuman Garhi
body: Hanuman Garhi, a temple complex on the southern edge of town near Tallital, is known for its sunset view over the plains. The observatory at nearby Manora Peak (ARIES) has organised night-sky programmes at times; check before you go.

items.name: Browse the Tibetan market and try local food
body: The Tibetan market near Mallital sells woollens, jackets and souvenirs. Nainital's food is simple: momos and thukpa, bun-tikki, and baked goods. Look for Kumaoni dishes such as bhatt ki churkani and aloo ke gutke in local eateries, and bal mithai, a speciality of nearby Almora, in sweet shops.

items.name: Bhimtal, Sattal and Naukuchiatal
body: Bhimtal, 22 km away, is larger than Naini Lake and has an island aquarium. Naukuchiatal, the nine-cornered lake, offers paragliding and quiet stays. Sattal is a cluster of seven small lakes in dense forest, good for birdwatching, kayaking and camping. The three are easily combined in one day.

items.name: Mukteshwar
body: Mukteshwar, about 50 km away, is a quiet orchard town with a hilltop Shiva temple, Chauli ki Jali cliffs and views of the high Himalaya. It is also a base for rock climbing and rappelling.

items.name: Kainchi Dham and Ranikhet
body: Kainchi Dham, the ashram of Neem Karoli Baba, lies on the road towards Almora and draws many visitors. Ranikhet, a cantonment town with golf links and pine forests, is about two hours away.

items.name: See snow in winter
body: Nainital gets snowfall in some winters, usually between late December and February, when the ridges and rooftops turn white. It is not guaranteed; check forecasts and road conditions before you go.

byTraveller.text: Boating, the ropeway, the Eco Cave Gardens, the zoo and Bhimtal's aquarium keep children busy. Avoid peak summer weekends if you can.
An early boat on the lake, the walk to Tiffin Top, a quiet stay at Sattal or Naukuchiatal and an evening on the Mall.
Nainital is about seven to eight hours from Delhi by road; the overnight train to Kathgodam is a comfortable alternative.

oneDay: Take a boat on Naini Lake in the morning and visit the Naina Devi Temple. Ride the ropeway to Snow View, then have lunch on the Mall. In the afternoon walk to Tiffin Top or visit the Eco Cave Gardens, and end the day strolling the Mall Road.
tips: Kathgodam, about 35 km away, is the nearest railway station; Pantnagar is the nearest airport.
Weekends, summer holidays and long weekends are extremely busy, with traffic jams and hotel shortages; weekdays are much calmer.
Carry warm layers year-round; evenings are cool even in summer and it can snow in winter.
Parking is limited; many hotels ask you to park at designated lots.

faqs.q: What are the best things to do in Nainital?
faqs.a: Go boating on Naini Lake, visit Naina Devi Temple, walk the Mall Road, ride the ropeway to Snow View, walk to Tiffin Top, hike Naina Peak and take a day trip to Bhimtal, Sattal and Naukuchiatal.

faqs.q: How many days are enough for Nainital?
faqs.a: Two days covers the lake, Mall Road and viewpoints. Three to four days lets you explore the nearby lakes and Mukteshwar.
Yes. Boating, the ropeway, the Eco Cave Gardens and the zoo are popular with children, and hotels cater well to families.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Nainital?
faqs.a: March to June for pleasant weather, and October to November for clear Himalayan views. Winter can bring snow; the monsoon brings heavy rain and landslide risk.
In some years, usually between late December and February. Snowfall is not guaranteed, and higher spots such as Naina Peak and Kilbury are more likely to see it.
